articles.title: Caleb Downs, Cowboys’ defense will stick it to detractors in Week 1
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys have some issues with their offensive line, but believers in the team have been growing. However, not everybody has bought in. But Caleb...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys have some issues with their offensive line, but believers in the team have been growing . However, not everybody has bought in. But Caleb Downs and the Cowboys' defense will stick it to detractors in Week 1 and finish top-10 in 2026.

With Tyler Smith headed to IR for at least a month, the Cowboys will have to juggle their offensive line. But that won't be a problem for this juggernaut offense. The Cowboys will still score plenty of points.

The question has been all offseason: What will the defense do?

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Cowboys' defense primed to have a big year

It's not a matter of trying to be middle of the pack. The Cowboys are aiming higher. And they should. They have talented players all over the revamped unit. And new coordinator Christian Parker is the right choice to get them in the right positions to make plays.

One of the main reasons the Cowboys will be good is Downs. He's going to be a stud, beginning in Week 1. Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will undoubtedly serve Downs an interception.

But it starts up front for the Cowboys with Quinnen Williams , according to The Athletic.

"This is a well-coached, well-built team with elite talent at multiple premium positions — most specifically: quarterback, receiver, and defensive tackle (I would count Quinnen Williams as the rare example of an interior defensive lineman in the "premium position" category)," Jourdan Rodrigue wrote.

"Defensively, the vision to significantly raise the floor is clear despite remaining questions about personnel. One of the best qualities a Super Bowl contender has is that it knows what it is, and knows what it is not (and can adjust to mask that). I don't yet know whether Dallas is a Super Bowl contender, but for once, it has this quality."

"While the offense has all the makings of a top-three unit, at least — Dak Prescott isn't thinking top three, he's thinking No. 1 — it's the other side of the ball that offers real opportunity," Zak Keefer wrote. "Jerry and Stephen Jones were so impressed with Christian Parker in the interview process that they broke out of their comfort zone and hired a first-time coordinator. For years, without exception, Dallas recycled former head coaches for that role.

"With some much-needed additions, starting with first-round pick Caleb Downs , this unit should be far more respectable this season. Paired with an elite offense, that could translate into three or four more wins."

Downs is going to make a lot of NFL general managers look silly. Here is the list of teams: Jets , Cardinals, Giants, Chiefs , Commanders (especially the Commanders), and Saints .

All of those teams passed on Downs. None of them should have. No matter the makeup of their team. And the Commanders likely made the biggest gaffe of all. They needed Downs. But they chose linebacker Sonny Styles . We've already seen in the preseason how it looks like a bad decision. It will likely end with Dan Quinn seeking employment elsewhere.

But it's the Cowboys' gain. And Downs is going to cut loose.

The Cowboys do have a few things that need to fall into place. They need DeMarvion Overshown to stay healthy. They need Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku to rush the passer effectively. Or they need Malachi Lawrence to excel as a rookie. Or perhaps Von Miller can turn back the clock and give them enough snaps on the edge.

It's a tough road ahead for teams that play the Cowboys. It's going to be tough to score 20-24 points against this defense. Good luck trying to keep the Cowboys from getting 28 or more.

Wins are the main thing. And the Cowboys will get those. It will likely start with a brutal beatdown of the Giants. Sure, the Cowboys may have some Week 1 hiccups with Parker getting his feet wet. But it shouldn't impact the bottom line.

"If the Cowboys are going to reach their goals, Parker has to be to Dallas what Steve Spagnuolo was to the 2007 New York Giants ," Jonathan Jones wrote. "It's been done before, and it will be done again. The hype around Christian Parker is real. Philadelphia knew it would lose him and still hated to see him leave.

"The Cowboys immediately involved him in free agency and draft prep. As much as you can invest in a 34-year-old stranger from a division rival to turn around your defense, Dallas has."

The defense is here. The Super Bowl hopes are real.

It's true that the defense doesn't have to stand out for the team to win games. That's because the offense believes it can score on any possession. The right pieces are in place, according to The Athletic.

"I mean it's definitely different," said Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. "I'm optimistic going into every season kind of with that mindset. It's an NFL season. Positive vibes and good energy doesn't win you games. So, understanding that we've put ourselves in a great position. We put ourselves right where we need to be to go and give ourselves the best chance to have a great week of practice and win Week 1 up there in New York.

"Right now, the energy and everything is great, but we got to make sure we're doing everything to be accountable to each other and just continue on that trajectory. We've got to go do it. We've got to go win games."

articles.summary: Patriots WR A.J. Brown to miss at least four weeks because of Week 1 injury
articles.body:

articles.body:
Florida A&M football has been forced to make a quarterback change after starter Isaiah Knowles was ruled out for the season with a thumb injury .

Backup Dustin Fletcher led the Rattler offense on the field for their first possession against the Miami Hurricanes on Thursday, Sept. 10, for a Week 2 "money game" at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens.

Fletcher replaces Knowles, who left Sept. 6's 31-13 Orange Blossom Classic loss against the third quarter after hurting his right throwing hand after taking a hit from a South Carolina State defender. Fletcher subbed in and completed 6-of-8 passes for 68 yards.

And now, he's responsible for operating head coach Quinn Fordham Gray Sr.'s offense against the defending College Football Playoff runners-up and No. 7-ranked team in the USA TODAY top 25 .

Who is FAMU football quarterback Dustin Fletcher ?

Fletcher transferred to the Rattlers from The Citadel .

The graduate student from Flint, Michigan, also previously played at Northern Illinois.

Out of Carman-Ainsworth High School, Fletcher set every single passing record for the Cavaliers. He was ranked as one of the top 30 high school quarterbacks in the nation and No. 1 in Michigan as an all-state selection.

Fletcher was a summertime commit for the Orange and Green and was named the second-string quarterback behind Knowles when FAMU released its initial depth chart for August's season opener against Albany State , a game in which he also appeared in briefly.

The remaining quarterbacks on FAMU's roster are James Hayes, Dante Howell, and Armond Parker.

articles.title: Mad Hatters: deGrom and Gilbert duel, Julio brings a missile launcher in 4-3 win
articles.summary: Mariners outlast deGrom, win series over Rangers thanks to big blast from Julio Rodríguez
articles.body:
So often pitchers' duels don't really stand up to the hype, but today's matchup between two former Stetson Hatters – the Mariners' Logan Gilbert and the Rangers' Jacob deGrom – delivered on all that promise and then some. The two pitchers combined for 23 strikeouts, and deGrom carried a perfect game through five innings. In true pitching duel style, it looked like the pitcher who blinked first would come out on the short end, but despite Logan Gilbert making a couple of mistakes, his offense was able to pick him up and deliver him the win. Bragging rights are fun; wins are better. (Gilbert also gets the honor of leading MLB in whiffs today: 24 to deGrom's 20, despite having one fewer strikeout than deGrom.)

This all being said, it was a slog for the Mariners early on. The best at-bat the first time through the order for the Mariners went to – surprise, surprise – Cal Raleigh , who battled deGrom for nine pitches before striking out on deGrom's fastest fastball of the day, a 99.6 mph heater (my campaign for decimal points on the ribbon board in the stadium, which read 100, continues unabated). But the Mariners did fight deGrom, getting themselves into good counts and forcing him into the zone; he finished the second inning at 37 pitches, compared to Gilbert's 24.

But it only took two pitches to offset that work in the third. Nicky Lopez was able to take 96 up and in from Gilbert and find a hole on the infield, and one batter later, with two outs, Joc Pederson jumped a first-pitch slider for a two-run homer. It wasn't a terrible pitch from Gilbert, away from Pederson but probably still too much on the plate; Gilbert had struck Pederson out on the slider in his first at-bat. The slider was particularly nasty today, with an eye-popping 75% whiff rate. He led with the pitch, throwing it 40 times, 12 times to start off an at-bat, which feels like a different sequence than he's used. Gilbert credits Cal for coming up with a good game plan, especially after he felt like he fell into some predictable patterns in his last time out against the A's.

"Like with Joc, we got him with the slider early, so he probably thought we were going to it next time," explained Gilbert. "But then also other guys, we went heavy spin, like with Duran, and then next time went three or four straight fastballs. So I think we did a good job there. They're trying to look at how we're probably scouting them, and then next time through, maybe pitch them different. I think Cal did a good job there."

But deGrom was just as tough on the other side. After striking out eight times in the first three innings, the Mariners hitters decided to try a different strategy the second time through the order. That also didn't work, as they let deGrom cruise through the fourth on nine pitches, keeping his perfect game intact.

Unfortunately, in a game that was all about which pitcher would blink first, Gilbert blinked both first and second. He made a mistake to start the fifth, hitting Evan Carter with a slider; Carter went on to steal second and then take third on an erroneous throw by Cal Raleigh, essentially making that hit by pitch a leadoff triple. Gilbert seemed to lose focus after that, walking Jake Burger after striking him out earlier, and then the Rangers were able to small-ball in a run on a bunt from Nicky Lopez that turned into a base hit when Gilbert couldn't field the weak dribbler cleanly. Nine-hole hitter Danny Jansen then bunted the runners into scoring position, but that strategy backfired as Pederson hit into a fielder's choice on a soft grounder to Naylor, erasing the runner trying to come home, and then the Rangers tried to get overly aggressive on a wild pitch from Gilbert that bounced hard off the brick backstop and directly to Cal Raleigh, where he was able to tag out Lopez trying to come home.

Finally in the sixth inning Cole Young , Perfect Boy, broke up the perfect game; in an 0-2 count he cracked a ball that glanced off deGrom's glove for an infield single and then scampered to second on a wild pitch. Young spoke yesterday after his big double about how he feels like in September he's been trying to simplify things and just focus on putting the ball in play, and he did do that here. Thank you for saving me from having to write up deGrom's perfecto, Cole, you have never been more My Favorite than you are right now.

"Obviously, I knew the perfect game was going, so I just wanted to put the ball in play," said Young postgame. "I kind of got lucky there with it hitting off his glove and then bouncing in a dead zone, so I was able to get that hit. But just trying to get on the fastball and put it in play, honestly."

The Rangers threatened again in the seventh, with Gilbert still out there; Langford led off with a walk and the Rangers made productive outs to get him to third, which brought up Lopez with two outs. With Logan pushing into the upper 90s in his pitch count, he spiked a splitter, and Langford broke for home aggressively. Cal was able to recover the ball, though, and made a nice toss to his long-term batterymate; Gilbert smacked down the tag on Langford to save a run and earn perpetual bragging rights among the starters. This is unironically one of my favorite clips of the year; I could watch it all day. (What is Logan saying there? I think it's "it's in my glove" but I can't tell.)

Your browser does not support the video tag. Download the video .

With deGrom finally out of the game in the seventh, the Mariners made their move. Jakob Junis started off the inning by hitting Randy, never a smart move; he then advanced to second on a wild pitch. Dominic Canzone then briefly got to hold the title of WPA leader for the day, knocking in Arozarena with a solid ground ball single and ensuring the Mariners wouldn't get shut out. Cal Raleigh followed that up with a single, extending his on-base streak to 12 games.

With Julio up to bat, Junis tried to sneak a first-pitch sinker past him. It's been a struggle at the plate lately for Julio, but this sinker arrived right in Julio's – to use a Ryon Healy-approved term – honey hole.

"I thought that ball was going to go through the back net in the bullpen," said manager Dan Wilson postgame. "There was no way the ballpark could contain it because it was just hit so hard…As we've said before, this game rewards you when you do things right, and he's been putting in the work and got a big payoff today for that."

Julio was actually out for early work yesterday – something he doesn't always do – working on his swing with his longtime organizational scout and friend (and home run derby pitcher) Franmy Pena.

"I just feel like I'm focusing on getting back to my roots," said Julio about reconnecting with his old friend. "[Franmy] was someone who signed me to the Mariners. He helped me develop back then when I was a kid, and I just feel like I needed a little refresher on things and just getting back to who I am and the things I do well."

Gabe Speier posted a clean eighth in relief of Gilbert to keep the Mariners' lead alive, setting up Andrés Muñoz for the save. Muñoz retired his first two hitters on groundouts but then walked the righty Langford, setting up a battle with Evan Carter. But Muñoz couldn't reign in his command despite being able to use his changeup against the lefty, walking Carter and bringing up the power threat Burger. In a 2-2 count, Muñoz spotted a fastball at 101.2 on the outer edge that Burger was forced to swing at, grounding it right to the steadiest hand on the Mariners' infield, Cole Young, who both stepped on second to beat out Carter and completed the throw through to first to easily beat out the slow-footed Burger, essentially getting the third and fourth outs of the inning to secure the Mariners win and the series win.

"There's just so many different layers to that play," said Young. "I wanted to make sure it didn't hit the base and get past me, so making sure of that first, and then after I caught it I'm like, okay, I've got a chance at second, let's just go there. But I knew it was going to be a bang-bang play so I started running and he's approaching second and I'm like, oh, this could be close, I don't know if I got him, so I threw it to first to make sure. I knew we got him at first, so I wasn't worried, but it was definitely a really weird play."

(Postgame when the media was thanking Young for his time, Muñoz piped up from his neighboring locker: "yes, thank you , Cole.")

The math continues to not math in the Mariners' favor, with the Astros winning today as well, but what's done is done; bragging rights might not get you to the postseason but they are a nice comfort, and for all the times his offense hasn't helped him out, it's nice for Gilbert to get that big shiny W.

articles.title: Getting to know Oklahoma ahead of matchup vs Michigan
articles.summary: Here’s what you need to know about the Oklahoma Sooners ahead of their matchup vs Michigan.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners come to Ann Arbor for the first time in history. Oklahoma is 2-0 all-time versus Michigan , but will they remain undefeated after the game on Saturday?

Here's a look at Oklahoma ahead of the showdown against Michigan.

Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables won two national championships as defensive coordinator of Clemson and is considered one of the best defensive minds in the nation. Venables is 33-20 at Oklahoma but has struggled in bowl games, going 0-4. In Oklahoma's lone playoff appearance under Venables, they lost 34-24 to Alabama in the CFP First Round last season.

Oklahoma beat UTEP 51-0 last week, holding their opponent to 2-of-13 on third-down with just 198 yards of total offense. Oklahoma's offense had 401 total yards and quarterback John Mateer threw for three passing touchdowns.

Oklahoma could have one of the best QBs in the nation

John Mateer has the ability to be electric as a runner and a thrower. Mateer's production took a dip last year, throwing for 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions after a 2024 season at Washington State with 29 touchdowns and just seven picks. Part of Mateer's 'regression' in 2026 can be attributed to him playing much of the season at less than 100% after breaking his right thumb in September and only missing one game. Mateer's grip on the ball is back to what it should be, and he'll likely revert back to his 2024 form. Even if Mateer doesn't find success, he can gash a team running. Mateer had eight rushing scores last season for 431 yards.

Michigan head coach Kyle Whittingham on Oklahoma

"I can tell you right now, I've studied the personnel; they're very talented. Their defensive line is outstanding. Quarterback, we did a deep dive on him when he was at Washington State, when he went into the portal because we would have liked to have had him at Utah… he's a dual threat. A guy who can beat you both ways… They've got a game-breaking receiver… They are very talented in all three phases, and we've got our work cut out for us, big time."

Oklahoma beat Michigan 24-13 last season in Norman at Memorial Stadium. John Mateer had one passing touchdown and two rushing scores while Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood struggled, going just 9-of-22 for 142 yards. It was the first road start of Underwood's career.

Cole Sullivan looked like a promising young linebacker who could be on the path to being a great player at Michigan, but he transferred to Oklahoma this offseason and will now be taking on his former team.

"We say it's always just a nameless, faceless opponent, so that's what I'm going to do my best to treat it," Sullivan said . "Nothing's going to change in my preparation. Obviously, it's a special one, but nothing's going to change in my preparation as far as how I handle myself before the game or during the game."

Key player to watch on defense, special teams

Linebacker Kip Lewis is a tackling machine, leading the team last season with 76 tackles (10.5 for loss) with four sacks.

Receiver Isaiah Satenga returned a punt last week 88 yards for a touchdown and had 76 receiving yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
